text:
Victor Olofsson's second stint in Vegas has been a strange, productive one. He scored twice in Seattle on Oct. 6, left that game early and missed a month. Since coming back he has eight goals and 12 points in 11 games, five of them on the power play, and a Yahoo Sports headline called him "a driving force during second Vegas stint." His goal against Dallas on Nov. 19 came on the Mark Stone assist that made Stone the franchise's career points leader, as The Athletic's Jesse Granger noted.

Part of this is real. His ice time is up almost two minutes a night over his last ten games, and he's getting more chances (3.6 expected goals on his own shots, a measure of chance quality, against 2.8 usual). At five on five Vegas takes 67.4% of the expected goals with him on.

The finishing is the part to doubt. He is shooting 30% after 9% last season, split between Colorado and Calgary: eight goals on 3.7 expected. Evolving-Hockey also noted he played with strong teammates last season, which flatters raw numbers. Watch whether the chances hold up once the pucks stop going in.
headline: Victor Olofsson is back and finishing everything
